gallery.title: File:B+O 173 camelback locomotive.jpg
gallery.description: A 4-6-0 camelback locomotive built by the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad in 1873.  Photographed at the Museum of Transportation in St. Louis, Missouri.  This image is a composite of three photos taken in a series vertically in order to cover the whole machine in the cramped area of the shed where this loocmotive is housed.  The result is severe barrel distortion from the extremely short effective focal length produced by the process.  The original images were resized with ImageMagick and processed with hugin to create the composite, which was cropped with GIMP, which created the final jpeg file.  No other processing or modifications were done to produce this image.

gallery.filename: Burlington Zephyr dining car Museum of Transportation St. Louis.jpg
gallery.title: File:Burlington Zephyr dining car Museum of Transportation St. Louis.jpg
gallery.credit:
St. Louis - Burlington Zephyr Dining Car

Uploaded by We hope
gallery.source: Burlington Zephyr dining car Museum of Transportation St. Louis
gallery.description:
This Burlington Zephyr dining car Silver Spoon belongs to the National Museum of Transport in St. Louis.  It was part a later vintage of Zephyr trains, which had more conventional cars.  The original Burlington Zephyrs from the mid/late 1939s were fixed trainsets with a set of wheels joining each pair of cars, rather than each car having two sets of wheels. The Budd Company built this dining car in 1938; it seated 48 and was numbered as CB&Q #192.

The cars in the background were from other railroads, and would not have been part of a Zephyr.  The second might be Baltimore & Ohio.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 573 (5963069751).jpg
gallery.description: Wabash RR class "F-4" 2-6-0 No.573 (Rhode Island 3147 of 1899) at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70. 131 of these moguls of different classes (some simples, some compounds) were built: 24 F-4 simples by RI and Richmond Works in 1899, 4 F-5 compounds by RI and Richmond Works in 1899, 66 F-6 compounds by RI, Richmond Works and Baldwin 1901-03, and 37 F-7 simples by Baldwin in 1904. They were withdrawn 1927-55.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn "S" 0-6-0 (5963070371).jpg
gallery.description: Southern Pacific RR "S" Class 0-6-0 (number not known) at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70. The various "S" Classes were the standard Southern Pacific RR and Texas & New Orleans RR switcher, 138 being built for the former 1903-23 and 61 for the latter 1904-26, being built by SP, T&NO, Baldwin, ALCO & Lima.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 3695 (5963864160).jpg
gallery.description: Scullin Steel 0-6-0 switcher No.3695 built by Baldwin in 1956 at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 39 (5963627334).jpg
gallery.description: Boston & Albany 4-4-0 No.39 "Mamora" built 1876 with domeless boiler (the rectangular "dome" on the boiler being a sandbox). The class of which No.39 was a member were very reliable locos and nicknamed "Eddy Clocks" after theri designer, Wilson Eddy. At the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 7 (5963068751).jpg
gallery.description: Great Lakes Carbon fireless 0-4-0 No.7 at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70.

gallery.title: File:Aerotrain No.3 (5963068391).jpg
gallery.description: Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific RR EMD 11-car (including one power car) "Aerotrain" showing the 1,200 hp Bo-A power car of "Aerotrain No.3" at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70. 55 cars in 5 sets were built in 1955 for the Pensyvania RR, New York Central, Milwaukee and Union Pacific but  all were withdrawn by 1058 except two units which were sold to the C.R.I.&P. R.R. but which were themselves withdrawn in 1965. They were spectacular looking but failures owing to technical deficiencies and servicing difficulties whilst the passenger accomodation was very cramped, as I found when I entered a car.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 311 (5963625532).jpg
gallery.description: Missouri, Kansas, Texas RR "E3" Class 4-4-0 No.311, one of 12 built 1896 by MKT RR, rebuilt in 1923 with new oil-fired boiler and piston valves and eventually demoted from express passenger to branch mixed traffic duties in Oklahoma, not finally being withdrawn until 1945-50. At the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 2727 (5963069069).jpg
gallery.description: Chesapeake & Ohio RR "K4" Class "Berkshire" 2-8-4 No.2727, one of 90 built by ALCO and LIMA in 1943-47 at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70. All had cast steel beds and roller bearings on all axles whilst the last 5 had all welded boilers. What the strange, rather dilapidated, wooden structure is in the foreground I have no idea.

gallery.title: File:Hugh llewelyn 12 (5963626334).jpg
gallery.description: Alton & Southern RR 0-8-0 No.12, ALCO No.65952 of 1926, at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70. Though "only" an 0-8-0, the engine alone weighed no less than 125 tons and with tender the toral weight was 208 tons!
